They are queued for attestation. ⚠️ AMH'S OWN INSTRUCTION IS TO FOLLOW LOCAL PROTOCOL WHERE AVAILABLE, and that is carried as the guideline's first line. claims.claim: ⚠️ AMH'S OWN INSTRUCTION: FOLLOW LOCAL PROTOCOL WHERE AVAILABLE. Hypoglycaemia can occur in people with diabetes RECEIVING INSULIN OR SULFONYLUREAS
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Hypoglycaemia' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/endocrine-drugs/drugs-diabetes/drugs-hypoglycaemia/hypoglycaemia, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: MILD HYPOGLYCAEMIA will respond to ORAL GLUCOSE OR SUCROSE (cane sugar). ⚠️ GIVE GLUCOSE -- eg GLUCOSE TABLETS -- TO PEOPLE TREATED WITH ACARBOSE, BECAUSE OF DELAYED ABSORPTION OF SUCROSE
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Hypoglycaemia' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/endocrine-drugs/drugs-diabetes/drugs-hypoglycaemia/hypoglycaemia, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: SEVERE HYPOGLYCAEMIA IN AN ADULT UNABLE TO TAKE ORAL FOOD OR FLUIDS: SC OR IM GLUCAGON, OR IV INFUSION OF 15-20 g GLUCOSE -- WHICH IS 150-200 mL OF GLUCOSE 10%, OR 75-100 mL OF GLUCOSE 20% INJECTION
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Hypoglycaemia' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/endocrine-drugs/drugs-diabetes/drugs-hypoglycaemia/hypoglycaemia, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ ALTERNATIVELY GLUCOSE 50% INJECTION MAY BE USED -- GIVE BY SLOW IV INJECTION INTO A SECURE IV CANNULA IN AN ANTECUBITAL VEIN TO REDUCE THE RISK OF SUPERFICIAL THROMBOPHLEBITIS
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Hypoglycaemia' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/endocrine-drugs/drugs-diabetes/drugs-hypoglycaemia/hypoglycaemia, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: IN CHILDREN with severe hypoglycaemia, GIVE GLUCAGON OR IV GLUCOSE 10% INJECTION and FOLLOW LOCAL PROTOCOL. ⚠️ MONITOR CLOSELY -- CONTINUED GLUCOSE BOLUSES MAY RENDER A YOUNG CHILD HYPEROSMOLAR, WITH THE RISK OF CEREBRAL OEDEMA
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Hypoglycaemia' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/endocrine-drugs/drugs-diabetes/drugs-hypoglycaemia/hypoglycaemia, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: RESPONSE SHOULD OCCUR WITHIN 10 MINUTES FOR GLUCAGON AND WITHIN 4-5 MINUTES FOR GLUCOSE. ⚠️ WHEN THE PERSON HAS RESPONDED, GIVE LONGER-ACTING CARBOHYDRATES -- eg A SANDWICH -- TO PREVENT RECURRENT HYPOGLYCAEMIA
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Hypoglycaemia' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/endocrine-drugs/drugs-diabetes/drugs-hypoglycaemia/hypoglycaemia, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: ⚠️ PROLONGED TREATMENT WITH GLUCOSE INFUSION MAY BE REQUIRED FOR HYPOGLYCAEMIA DUE TO A LONG-ACTING SULFONYLUREA. OCTREOTIDE MAY BE USED IF HYPOGLYCAEMIA PERSISTS DESPITE GLUCOSE INFUSION
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, 'Hypoglycaemia' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/endocrine-drugs/drugs-diabetes/drugs-hypoglycaemia/hypoglycaemia, July 2026 release ('Last modified by AMH: July 2026'), read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Nonsevere hypoglycaemia in a conscious adult: glucose 15 g orally (about 20 g if glucose under 3 mmol/L), recheck after 10-15 minutes and repeat if still under 4 mmol/L; seek advice if 3 or more portions needed; then a longer-acting carbohydrate. Children: 5 g (5 years or younger/up to 25 kg) or 10 g (6 years+/over 25 kg). Patients on acarbose must use glucose, not sucrose.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Diabetes guideline: 'Hypoglycaemia in patients with diabetes' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Diabetes&topicfile=hypoglycaemia-in-patients-with-diabetes, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Nonsevere hypoglycaemia in patients with diabetes'

claims.claim: Minidose glucagon for children with type 1 diabetes when oral glucose impractical: 20 micrograms SC/IM if 2 years or younger; 10 micrograms per year of age up to 150 micrograms for 3-15 years; double if no rise at 30 minutes; may repeat after 2-3 hours.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Diabetes guideline: 'Hypoglycaemia in patients with diabetes' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Diabetes&topicfile=hypoglycaemia-in-patients-with-diabetes, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Minidose glucagon injection'

claims.claim: After severe hypoglycaemia in adults: check glucose every 1-2 hours for 4 hours; warn of recurrence risk within 24-48 hours; no driving until cleared by a diabetes specialist.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Diabetes guideline: 'Hypoglycaemia in patients with diabetes' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Diabetes&topicfile=hypoglycaemia-in-patients-with-diabetes, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Severe hypoglycaemia in patients with diabetes'

claims.claim: Nonsevere hypoglycaemia does not justify withholding insulin; never stop insulin in type 1 diabetes, but review dose.
claims.locator: Therapeutic Guidelines (eTG complete), Diabetes guideline: 'Hypoglycaemia in patients with diabetes' at https://app.tg.org.au/viewTopic?etgAccess=true&guidelinePage=Diabetes&topicfile=hypoglycaemia-in-patients-with-diabetes, accessed 2026-09-24 through the owner's subscription, section 'Follow-up after nonsevere hypoglycaemia'
